Package neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.propertygenerator

Class OlgaTableGridFiller

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.propertygenerator.OlgaTableGridFiller
final class OlgaTableGridFiller extends Object
Grid post-processing shared by the OLGA PVT table generators.

An OLGA table has a gas column and a liquid column at every (pressure, temperature) node, but a flash only returns the phases that actually exist. At a node where one phase is absent the generators have no value to write, and writing zero is not an option: OLGA rejects the file outright with OIL DENSITY IS ZERO AT ... or the gas equivalent, so a single-phase fluid produced a table that could not be loaded at all.

The absent-phase nodes are therefore filled by nearest-neighbour extrapolation from the nodes where the phase does exist, measured in grid-index space. This is the same convention commercial table generators use: outside the two-phase region the absent phase's properties are held at the boundary value so the table stays loadable and continuous, and OLGA never evaluates them for a phase whose mass fraction is zero.

1.0

    • fillAbsentNodes

      static int fillAbsentNodes(double[][] values, boolean[][] present, double fallback)
      Replace values at absent-phase nodes by the nearest node where the phase exists.

      Distance is the Manhattan distance in grid indices, which makes the fill independent of the pressure and temperature units and of the grid spacing.

      Parameters:
      values - property values indexed [pressure][temperature], modified in place
      present - true where the phase exists and the value is usable
      fallback - value written when the phase exists nowhere on the grid
      Returns:
      number of nodes that were filled

    • fillAlongAxis

      static boolean[][] fillAlongAxis(double[][] values, double[][] gradient, boolean[][] present, double[] coordinates, boolean alongTemperature, boolean logarithmic, double minimumFraction)
      Fill absent-phase nodes along one grid axis so the column stays monotonic and continuous.

      Along each grid line, a gap between two nodes where the phase exists is linearly interpolated, and nodes beyond the last existing node are extrapolated with the phase's own gradient there: density along pressure with dRho/dP, enthalpy along temperature with Cp, entropy along temperature with Cp ln(T). A missing or non-positive gradient is replaced by the secant through the two outermost existing nodes, and by a flat extension if that is not positive either. Lines without any existing node are left for fillAbsentNodes(double[][], boolean[][], double).

      Parameters:
      values - property values indexed [pressure][temperature], modified in place
      gradient - gradient of the property along the axis at the same nodes, may be null
      present - true where the phase exists and the value is usable
      coordinates - axis coordinates, Pa for pressure and K for temperature
      alongTemperature - true to fill along temperature, false along pressure
      logarithmic - true to integrate the gradient against ln(coordinate), used for entropy
      minimumFraction - lower bound on an extrapolated value as a fraction of its anchor, or 0 for no bound
      Returns:
      presence mask extended with the filled nodes

    • monotonicFill

      static boolean[][] monotonicFill(String keyword, String[] keywords, double[][][] props, boolean[][] present, double[] pressuresPa, double[] temperaturesK)
      Apply the gradient-based monotonic fill to a density, enthalpy or entropy column.

      Density is filled along pressure with its dRho/dP column, enthalpy and entropy along temperature with the phase heat capacity column. Other columns are returned unchanged for nearest-neighbour filling.

      Parameters:
      keyword - column keyword
      keywords - all column keywords of the table
      props - all column values indexed [column][pressure][temperature]
      present - phase-existence mask of the column
      pressuresPa - grid pressures [Pa]
      temperaturesK - grid temperatures [K]
      Returns:
      presence mask extended with the nodes filled here
